title: Trustworthy Medical Question Answering: An Evaluation-Centric Survey

bias_targets.methodology: Using paired prompts that differ only in demographic details (e.g., 'male patient' vs. 'female patient') to detect discrepancies in content, confidence, or thoroughness, and utilizing human evaluation rubrics in benchmarks like EquityMedQA.
Evaluating model responses using race-focused query sets, calculating group-wise accuracy gaps, and assessing human evaluation rubrics to measure disparities (e.g., via EquityMedQA).
Measuring response disparities across different geographies using adversarial datasets and human evaluation rubrics in benchmarks like EquityMedQA.
Assessing whether the system's performance is equitable across diverse user groups and contexts involving socioeconomic factors, utilizing qualitative bias annotations and clinician-led reviews.
Using condition-focused query sets and clinician-led reviews to flag stereotypes or inequitable treatment based on specific patient health conditions.
Introducing common clinically relevant cognitive biases into USMLE questions (e.g., via the BiasMedQA benchmark) through bias-laden prompts to test if user inputs distort model outputs.
